From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

## Headline Points

1. **The Seller Update contradicts the Seller's own Disclosure Letter on several issues.**
   - **Bluefen:** the Update says the consent is "addressed." The Disclosure Letter (DL §2) says no consent has been obtained.
   - **Riverlark:** the Update offers a release "following Completion." DL §3 says the facility has not been repaid or discharged.
   - **Privacy incident:** the Update calls it "not expected to be material." DL §6 says the investigation is still preliminary.
   - **Sandbar renewals:** the Update calls them "ordinary course." DL §8 expressly does not say so.

   We should rely on the Disclosure Letter, not the Update's summaries.
2. **Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 13 and 20.5 work together to collapse all protection into one capped regime.** As drafted, they reach fraud, title, tax and specific indemnities. Fixing this structure (SPA-N-014) is the main priority, ahead of the numbers.
3. **Several items are money that should come off the price.** Riverlark is about AUD 3.2m. The bonuses are AUD 420k plus on-costs. The renewals may be another AUD 330k. These should be handled through the debt-free/cash-free mechanics, not left to capped warranty claims.

---

## Issue-by-Issue

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer should want:** a higher general cap, for example 30–50% (AUD 7.2m–12m). Separately, fundamental warranties capped at 100% of price, specific indemnities outside the general cap, and fraud uncapped.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 40%. Be prepared to accept 20–25% only if the carve-outs below are agreed, or if W&I insurance sits above the cap.
- **Reason:** 20% is defensible only if title, tax, the specific indemnities and fraud all sit outside it, and the current draft caps everything.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis and AUD 250k basket (about 1.04% of price), with only the excess above the basket recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:** de minimis of about AUD 10–15k; basket of about AUD 120k (0.5%). A **tipping** basket, so the full amount is recoverable once the basket is exceeded. Related claims aggregated for de minimis. None of these thresholds to apply to fundamental, tax, specific indemnity or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** Counter with a tipping basket at 0.5% and allow aggregation of related claims.
- **Reason:** An excess-only basket at about 1% permanently absorbs AUD 250k of loss, and without aggregation a related series of small claims could escape entirely.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion, with the general limitation applying to all Claims unless stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - 24 months for general warranties, so the period covers two full audit cycles.
  - Tax: the ATO amendment period plus 3–6 months, or 5–7 years.
  - Fundamental: 6 years or more (consistent with the NSW *Limitation Act 1969* period for contract).
  - Fraud: no limit.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months, and reverse the default so that the 18–24 month limit applies only to general warranties.
- **Reason:** 18 months is at the low end of market, and the "applies to all" default quietly cuts the life of tax and title claims short.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime**
- **Seller:** capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limit as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:** fundamental warranties capped at 100% of price, with a time limit of at least 6 years. No de minimis, basket or disclosure against them, and no knowledge qualifier.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller's position.
- **Reason:** If the Seller cannot deliver title, the Buyer has lost AUD 24m, so recovery capped at AUD 4.8m makes no commercial sense.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature." There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer should want:** an express carve-out so that none of the limitations, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance provisions apply to fraud, wilful misconduct or deliberate concealment by the Seller or its representatives. Also an express preservation of rights under the ACL / misleading conduct.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. This is non-negotiable.
- **Reason:** Courts are reluctant to let a party contract out of its own fraud, but we should not leave this to litigation. The carve-out is universally market.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records (DL §1.1–1.2). DL §1.4 also contains a non-admission.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Specific disclosure only, against identified warranties, with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter.
  - No general data room disclosure, or at most data room documents limited to matters fairly disclosed in them.
  - No disclosure against fundamental warranties, tax warranties or specific indemnities.
  - Public records limited to searches of named registers on a stated date.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure.
- **Reason:** As drafted, any document buried in the data room would defeat any warranty, including the warranties we are relying on for the known issues.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** no claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew of, "including any matter discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** an express pro-sandbagging clause, so that Buyer knowledge does not reduce claims. As a fallback, a qualifier limited to the actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals of matters that were Disclosed, with no constructive or "discoverable" knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** Constructive knowledge combined with general disclosure would effectively remove most warranty protection for matters we have diligenced.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** reasonable endeavours, with the consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. DL §2 confirms no consent yet, and the clause 11.3 conditions are unsatisfied.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A condition precedent of an unconditional written consent under clause 11.2, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, with all clause 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived.
  - The CP to be waivable by the **Buyer only**.
  - A Seller obligation to use all reasonable endeavours.
  - A walk right or price renegotiation if the consent is not obtained by the sunset date.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller's mechanism and make this a hard condition precedent.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (about AUD 3.6m), and a bare consent letter with open conditions could still allow Bluefen to terminate.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** release to be provided after Completion. DL §3 says the facility (about AUD 3.2m) is unrepaid and the security undischarged.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A payout letter before Completion, and the facility repaid out of the purchase price through the funds flow, treated as Debt.
  - At Completion: executed deeds of release, PPSR financing change statements (or an undertaking to lodge them immediately), and return of title documents.
  - A specific indemnity for any residual amount owing.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release and make release a Completion deliverable.
- **Reason:** The price is on a debt-free basis, and if the release comes later the Buyer owns a company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and change-of-control default risk under clause 8.1.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** the AUD 420k is "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow (DL §5). The Seller is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:** the bonuses treated as Transaction Costs or Debt-like Items, including employer payroll tax, superannuation (if it applies to the bonus), workers' compensation and other on-costs. These amounts to be deducted from the price and shown in the funds flow, paid through Company payroll with PAYG withheld. A specific indemnity for any shortfall.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** The Company, not the Seller, is the legal payer and faces the tax liability, so leaving the bonuses out of the funds flow transfers at least AUD 420k to the Buyer.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** the indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is said to be adequate. DL §4: Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment; AUD 180k is open; there is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - As a Completion deliverable: evidence of payment in full plus an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay.
  - Failing that, an amount held back in escrow (at least AUD 180k plus a buffer).
  - A broadened indemnity covering failure to obtain ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials, third-party infringement claims, re-development or licensing costs, and business interruption. The indemnity should sit outside the cap, threshold and disclosure regime.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the limited indemnity.
- **Reason:** The real risk is not owning the IP, and the AUD 180k fee is only one part of that risk.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material." DL §6: about 1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and whether notification is required are all unknown.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Before Completion: a completed assessment under the Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, including the outcome of the "reasonable steps to assess" process within 30 days, and evidence of steps to retrieve or delete the file.
  - Any required OAIC and individual notifications made.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the general cap, thresholds and disclosure, for regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, and third-party and customer claims (including any Bluefen fallout).
  - A retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller's characterisation and require an uncapped (or separately capped) specific indemnity.
- **Reason:** The facts disclosed as at 22 September, now about 6 weeks old, suggest the 30-day assessment window may already have passed, so regulatory exposure may already exist. **Raise this urgently with the Seller.**

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are said to be ordinary-course costs. DL §8 asks for them to be "read together" and does not say they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Full copies of the contracts and an explanation of why one supply was split into three.
  - Confirmation of whether the split avoided a board approval or conduct-of-business threshold.
  - Any amounts that are unaccrued or non-ordinary-course treated as Debt-like Items, or terminated at the Seller's cost.
  - A specific warranty that the renewals were entered on arm's-length, ordinary-course terms.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label without diligence. Hold the issue open and treat the amounts as debt-like by default.
- **Reason:** Three linked AUD 110k contracts look like a single AUD 330k commitment split to stay below a threshold.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer should want:** a separately defined regime for each of the following, with the general limitations applying **only** to General Warranty Claims:
  1. general warranties;
  2. fundamental warranties;
  3. tax warranties and the tax indemnity;
  4. each specific indemnity (Ironquay, incident, bonuses, Riverlark);
  5. fraud.

  Exclusive remedy and non-reliance should also be carved out for categories 2 to 5.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. This is the structural priority.
- **Reason:** The default rule pulls every other protection under the AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month limit, which makes the fixes on N-004, N-005, N-011 and N-012 ineffective.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** title is said to be evidenced by the share register at DD-012. DL §10 states that this is only the source relied on, and that the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Our own ASIC company search and share structure history.
  - A full chain of issues and transfers since incorporation, with share certificates.
  - A PPSR search against the Seller and the shares.
  - Confirmation that there are no options, convertibles or employee equity entitlements.
  - The constitution and any shareholders' deed, to check for pre-emptive rights.
  - At Completion: share certificates, a signed transfer, and releases of any security.
  - The title warranty treated as fundamental (see N-004).
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone.
- **Reason:** A register is only prima facie evidence, and a capped title warranty combined with unverified title is the worst-case risk in the deal.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** treated as "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Tax: a stand-alone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, covering payroll tax on the bonuses, income tax, GST and any Division 7A or related-party issues. Tax warranties with their own time limit (see N-003), outside the basket and disclosure, with a cap up to 100% of price.
  - IP: specific IP warranties on ownership, non-infringement, open source and employee and contractor assignments, with an elevated cap, since Ironquay shows that the Company's IP chain has gaps.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled." Both remain open terms for our mark-up.
- **Reason:** The core value of an analytics business sits in its tax position and its IP, and the general regime gives inadequate protection for both.

---

## Other Items to Confirm (not in scope, but flagged)

- **Office lease (DL §7) and Mossvale (DL §9):** the Seller says these involve notification only, or an assignment restriction that is not triggered by a share sale. Have our counsel confirm this against the actual clauses, including any change-of-control definition. If confirmed, include a lease notification as a Completion deliverable.
- **Non-admission (DL §1.4):** this should not reduce the effect of any specific disclosure the Seller relies on. If it remains, require that disclosure be construed against the Seller.

## Suggested Next Steps

1. Send the Seller a short issues list now covering N-005, N-014 and N-012 (the notification timing).
2. Prepare a price and funds flow schedule deducting Riverlark, the bonuses and on-costs, and (provisionally) Sandbar.
3. Request information on Bluefen clause 11.3, the Ironquay payment evidence, the incident investigation file and the Sandbar contracts.
4. Decide on our W&I insurance strategy, since it will affect how hard we push on the N-001 to N-003 numbers.

*The percentages and periods above are typical market reference points for negotiating. NSW-qualified deal counsel should confirm the final positions.*

- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** The Company, not the Seller, is the legal payer and faces the tax liability, so leaving the bonuses out of the funds flow transfers at least AUD 420k to the Buyer.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** the indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is said to be adequate. DL §4: Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment; AUD 180k is open; there is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - As a Completion deliverable: evidence of payment in full plus an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay.
  - Failing that, an amount held back in escrow (at least AUD 180k plus a buffer).
  - A broadened indemnity covering failure to obtain ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials, third-party infringement claims, re-development or licensing costs, and business interruption. The indemnity should sit outside the cap, threshold and disclosure regime.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the limited indemnity.
- **Reason:** The real risk is not owning the IP, and the AUD 180k fee is only one part of that risk.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material." DL §6: about 1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and whether notification is required are all unknown.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Before Completion: a completed assessment under the Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, including the outcome of the "reasonable steps to assess" process within 30 days, and evidence of steps to retrieve or delete the file.
  - Any required OAIC and individual notifications made.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the general cap, thresholds and disclosure, for regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, and third-party and customer claims (including any Bluefen fallout).
  - A retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller's characterisation and require an uncapped (or separately capped) specific indemnity.
- **Reason:** The facts disclosed as at 22 September, now about 6 weeks old, suggest the 30-day assessment window may already have passed, so regulatory exposure may already exist. **Raise this urgently with the Seller.**

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are said to be ordinary-course costs. DL §8 asks for them to be "read together" and does not say they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Full copies of the contracts and an explanation of why one supply was split into three.
  - Confirmation of whether the split avoided a board approval or conduct-of-business threshold.
  - Any amounts that are unaccrued or non-ordinary-course treated as Debt-like Items, or terminated at the Seller's cost.
  - A specific warranty that the renewals were entered on arm's-length, ordinary-course terms.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label without diligence. Hold the issue open and treat the amounts as debt-like by default.
- **Reason:** Three linked AUD 110k contracts look like a single AUD 330k commitment split to stay below a threshold.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer should want:** a separately defined regime for each of the following, with the general limitations applying **only** to General Warranty Claims:
  1. general warranties;
  2. fundamental warranties;
  3. tax warranties and the tax indemnity;
  4. each specific indemnity (Ironquay, incident, bonuses, Riverlark);
  5. fraud.

  Exclusive remedy and non-reliance should also be carved out for categories 2 to 5.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. This is the structural priority.
- **Reason:** The default rule pulls every other protection under the AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month limit, which makes the fixes on N-004, N-005, N-011 and N-012 ineffective.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** title is said to be evidenced by the share register at DD-012. DL §10 states that this is only the source relied on, and that the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Our own ASIC company search and share structure history.
  - A full chain of issues and transfers since incorporation, with share certificates.
  - A PPSR search against the Seller and the shares.
  - Confirmation that there are no options, convertibles or employee equity entitlements.
  - The constitution and any shareholders' deed, to check for pre-emptive rights.
  - At Completion: share certificates, a signed transfer, and releases of any security.
  - The title warranty treated as fundamental (see N-004).
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone.
- **Reason:** A register is only prima facie evidence, and a capped title warranty combined with unverified title is the worst-case risk in the deal.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** treated as "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Tax: a stand-alone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, covering payroll tax on the bonuses, income tax, GST and any Division 7A or related-party issues. Tax warranties with their own time limit (see N-003), outside the basket and disclosure, with a cap up to 100% of price.
  - IP: specific IP warranties on ownership, non-infringement, open source and employee and contractor assignments, with an elevated cap, since Ironquay shows that the Company's IP chain has gaps.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled." Both remain open terms for our mark-up.
- **Reason:** The core value of an analytics business sits in its tax position and its IP, and the general regime gives inadequate protection for both.
